title: Lean and Mathlib communities certify Levent Alpöge's 17-million-line Lean proof of the Riemann Hypothesis (joint statement, Nov 21), endorsed by the Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative
author_or_publisher: Lean and Mathlib communities (Lean community blog)
quote_verbatim: We hereby certify that both the statement and the proof of the Riemann Hypothesis are correct.
what_is_new: Independent formal verification of the claimed proof (Run 39 item 012 logged it as unverified): dozens reproduced the build; comparator and con-leche confirm the theorem is exactly Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis; several kernels, some with formal soundness proofs, accepted the export, run on an inert export out of reach of possibly malicious proof code.
why_for_agiright: A landmark result reportedly produced by an Anthropic researcher working with Claude is now machine-checked: a hard data point for the AI research-acceleration debate (METR, Run 39), and a model for checking AI output that is too large for people to review.
doubts: The statement does not mention Claude or AI; the Claude/Anthropic link is from Run 39 sources and secondary reports (datastudios, Mint, Scientific American, seen in search only). An independent RIKEN build (shosonoda.github.io) reports a clean build, but its own Comparator run had no verdict when it was written. Also seen via Techmeme 2124382809225826694. Topics index searched: Riemann, Lean+Mathlib (no match).

title: Google DeepMind publishes the Gemini 4 Hydrogen Safety & Security Report: no CBRN or cyber CCL reached, but both CCL alert thresholds reached; AI control applied as if the stealth TCL were reached
quote_verbatim: Gemini 4 Hydrogen does not reach the CBRN or Cybersecurity CCLs, though it reaches the CCL alert thresholds for both domains
what_is_new: The full report the model card (topic-2026-000487) said was still to come: targeted CBRN and cyber tests only (lower capability than Argon under the Material Capability Change test); the stealth and situational-awareness TCL was not tested and control measures are applied as a precaution; sections on loss of control, agentic alignment, sycophancy and prompt injection.
why_for_agiright: A frontier lab reports alert thresholds reached and treats an untested loss-of-control threshold as reached: closes the Run 38/39 Hydrogen lead.
doubts: Release date unclear: the PDF metadata says created Nov 18, the server says last modified Nov 17 (GMT), and the model card page saved Nov 19 did not yet link it, so it is marked stale under the 48h rule. Linked from the blog.google Hydrogen post. Only the executive summary and FSF table were read (~6k of ~110k characters). Hydrogen went live in the Gemini app model selector on Nov 21 (testingcatalog; @OfficialLoganK, reposted by @demishassabis).

title: Techmeme (citing WSJ, sources): Alice Huang associate Li Ming, charged with fraud in Singapore in 2025, played a central role in getting restricted AI chips into China

what_is_new: Links the Singapore fraud case to Megaspeed and the wider NVIDIA-chip trade (Dmitri Alperovitch quotes WSJ: he took part in major decisions at Megaspeed). Same day: FT on an Alice Huang shell-company network (item 007).
why_for_agiright: Export-control enforcement on frontier AI chips, tied to the NVIDIA inquiries (House Dec 1-3, CA AG, SEC).
doubts: Owner rule 2026-11-12: Jensen Huang / NVIDIA matters are logged as governance, not gossip; this item is about chip-export enforcement, report-level. WSJ not opened (paywall); anonymous sources; no Singapore or US primary on the new claims.

title: Mustafa Suleyman on METR's capability update: eval science deserves frontier-scale funding and should probably soon be required by law
quote_verbatim: Eval science deserves frontier-scale funding. This should probably soon be something required by law.
what_is_new: A frontier-lab head (Microsoft AI) calls for legally required evaluation, quoting METR's 3.6-month doubling and its point that capabilities are getting harder to measure (Run 39 item 002).
why_for_agiright: An industry leader backs mandatory evaluation: relevant to the SAFE AI Act evaluator rules and California's independent-verification plans.
doubts: A personal post; no Microsoft policy document. What "this" should require by law is not spelled out.

title: Report body of the House China and Homeland Security joint report on PRC-developed open-weight models: Anysphere (Cursor) told the Committees it plans to explore phasing them out
author_or_publisher: House Committee on Homeland Security (Chairman Garbarino) and House Select Committee on China (Chairman Moolenaar)
quote_verbatim: Anysphere informed the Committees that it plans to explore phasing out PRC-developed open-weight models because of geopolitical risk.
what_is_new: Closes the Run 39 lead: the report body confirms the Cursor statement (Run 39 had it only from CNBC via Techmeme). Recommends removing PRC models from federal systems and contract work, a phased ban in high-risk critical infrastructure, and an American open-weight ecosystem.
why_for_agiright: Primary text for a report already on the site.
doubts: Found via web search (homeland.house.gov PDF). Marked stale because it predates the window start (released Nov 20). Summary and case-study sections read, not the full ~150k characters. The press release was logged in Run 39 (item 003).
